title: Nimbus load architect and customer SLA attestation
creator: Ava Mitchell
description: Purpose: Build and validate the Nimbus load architect — a focused load-testing harness and benchmark methodology to produce deterministic, repeatable throughput signatures and a customer acceptance test (CAT) workbook for Dedicated capacity SLAs. This ticket covers specification, harness implementation, benchmark protocol, telemetry contract, and an initial run with ACME Corp as a pilot customer. Objectives: 1) Define a canonical benchmark profile set (tenant mixes, prompt length distributions, model variants). 2) Implement Nimbus harness (traffic generator, KV priming, cold/warm start control, burst/resilience scenarios, autoscaler exercise). 3) Produce a signed throughput signature artifact and customer-facing CAT workbook with pass/fail gates. 4) Validate autoscaling policy observability and rollback/fallback behavior under constrained capacity. Out of scope: UI work in Console (separate PM ticket), long-term flakiness mitigation across thousands of tenants (follow-up epic).
acceptance_criteria: Nimbus harness can replay 3 canonical profiles deterministically with <2% variance in mean throughput across 5 runs
Measured tail latency p95/p99 curves match SLO band for committed capacity within tolerance defined in contract
Autoscaler exercise demonstrates correct scale-up within target time window and safe scale-down without request loss in 95% of runs
Generated customer CAT workbook includes step-by-step runbook, required inputs, expected telemetry queries (Grafana, BigQuery), and a signoff checklist
End-to-end artifacts (benchmark dataset, run logs, Grafana dashboards, GitHub PR) are uploaded and linked in the ticket
benchmark_methodology: Profile definitions: baseline (single-tenant steady QPS), mixed-tenant (70/20/10 heavy/medium/light), burst-microburst (sustained 10s bursts every 2m)
Token distribution: sample prompt lengths [16, 64, 256] and response lengths [32, 128] with weighted probabilities
Model variants: fp16 baseline, int8 quantized variant, and low-latency distilled model
KV priming: controlled warm-cache runs after deterministic priming sequence to measure warm vs cold behavior
Batching knobs: sweep of batch sizes and batching windows to produce cost vs latency curves
Autoscaler test steps: throttle node addition, artificial CPU/GPU pressure, and observe routing/fallback to burst pool
Metrics recorded: requests/sec, tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, queue length, batch size distribution, error rate, tail-queue-time
harness_implementation_notes: Nimbus is a small Rust harness with Python orchestration layer for scenario composition
Traffic generator supports tenant tags, request templates, and KV cache keys to exercise prefix caching
Integrates with existing telemetry pipeline: emits structured traces to X-Ray and metrics to Prometheus/Grafana export
Includes an opt-in mode to pump synthetic traces into the console tracing pipeline for correlation with production logs
Run configuration stored as YAML artifacts in the repo to ensure reproducibility
Produces a canonical CSV signature and an immutable run tarball (logs + telemetry + run manifests) for customer attestation
customer_acceptance_workbook: Pre-run checklist: capacity reservation, auth token for dedicated pool, baseline snapshot of config and model pins
Run steps: priming, baseline run, mixed-tenant run, burst run, autoscaler exercise, teardown
Verification queries: p95/p99 queries, throughput stability over 10 minute windows, CPU/GPU scaling timeline validation
Pass/fail gates: throughput delta <= contractual tolerance, error rate < 0.1%, no silent fallback to lower-tier model unless documented
Signoff rows: engineering lead, solutions engineer, customer technical contact, account manager
runbook_steps: Reserve dedicated pool and pin model versions
Deploy Nimbus harness to test runner namespace
Run KV priming sequence (prime.yaml) and confirm cache hit metrics
Execute baseline profile 5x and collect signatures
Execute mixed-tenant and burst profiles, exercise autoscaler
Collect telemetry, generate signature CSV, upload tarball to Drive
Run CAT verification queries and complete signoff checklist
results_summary: Pilot run with ACME Corp (2026-03-05): baseline throughput 12.3k tokens/sec, p95 latency 95ms, p99 320ms for quantized model
Warm cache improved throughput by ~28% and reduced p99 by ~40% in baseline profile
Autoscaler scale-up time median 28s (target <30s) but 2 runs showed slower cold-start >45s tied to model load step
Burst resilience: 4/6 runs passed resilient routing; two runs required manual intervention due to tenant tagging mismatch
Artifacts and CSV signatures uploaded; initial CAT workbook reviewed by Solutions Engineering and ACME SRE
open_issues: Investigate model load cold-start >45s on two runs (likely image pull + warmup sequencing) - follow-up with infra team
Make tenant tag enforcement stricter in harness to avoid routing mismatches
Add additional observer hooks during autoscaler scale-down to prevent premature kernel shutdown
Need a Console integration story for importing signature CSVs into customer dashboards (PM follow-up)
